summary: The material explains dosing in clinical language patients are unlikely to understand, buries the missed-dose instruction inside a dense paragraph, and opens with promotional text rather than the instruction itself.

findings.title: Dosing abbreviation BD never explained
findings.explanation_plain: BD means twice a day but is never defined in the text. A reader could take the wrong dose.
findings.recommendation: Write 'twice a day' or define BD at first use.

findings.title: Unexplained clinical terms
findings.explanation_plain: Clinical terms such as hyperkalaemia are used without any plain-language explanation.
findings.recommendation: Add a plain-language gloss the first time a clinical term is used.
findings.evidence: hyperkalaemia and deterioration of renal parameters

findings.title: No single clear main message up front
findings.explanation_plain: The page opens with promotional text rather than the medication instruction itself.
findings.recommendation: Lead with the instruction, not the marketing copy.
findings.evidence: The medication is to be taken as prescribed.

instrument_items.rationale: BD is used without definition anywhere in the material.
Sections between headings look short enough.
Specialized clinical terms are not explained at first use.

positive_observations: Storage and disposal instructions are itemized clearly.
